Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vegetarian' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Masculine: вегетарианец. Common feminine noun meaning 'vegetarian (female)' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ninetieth, nineties').

examples.trans: In the nineties there was no money at all.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.

meanings.note: Animate neuter noun. Common neuter noun meaning 'animal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я добрый человек, я люблю животных.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, pretty, handsome').

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.
